prompt: `WeekTests` is a `struct` with a stored `plan`. What does each test start from?
hint: Swift Testing makes a new instance per test.

choices.text: Whatever the previous test left in `plan`
choices.why: Each test gets its own instance, so nothing leaks between them.

choices.text: A new copy of that plan for every test
choices.why: Right: a new struct per test, and the property is the fixture.

choices.text: An empty plan, until `setUp()` fills it
choices.why: `setUp()` is XCTest's; Swift Testing uses the struct itself.

choices.text: The plan from `week/main.swift`
choices.why: The test target does not run the `week` program.

prompt: When should a test use `#require` rather than `#expect`?
hint: One stops the test, the other records and carries on.

choices.text: Always, since stopping early is faster
choices.why: Stopping hides the other expectations that also failed.

choices.text: When the rest would be meaningless
choices.why: Right: `try #require(plan.sessions.first)` ends cleanly on an empty plan.

choices.text: Only inside an XCTest test case
choices.why: `#require` is Swift Testing's; XCTest has its own functions.

choices.text: When comparing two strings rather than two numbers
choices.why: The type does not decide; whether to go on does.

prompt: In `countsOnlyTheWeekOfToday`, why are 110 minutes planned and not 155?
hint: Which Monday does `s3` belong to?

choices.text: `s3` is not done, so it is left out
choices.why: Planned counts done and not done alike; `s2` is not done and counts.

choices.text: A suite caps each total at 110
choices.why: Nothing caps a total; the dates decide.

choices.text: `s3`, on the 26th, is next week
choices.why: Right: 50 + 60 is this week's, and 45 belongs to the week of the 26th.

choices.text: Only sessions on or before today count
choices.why: `s2` is on the 23rd, after today, and counts.

prompt: How many tests did `swift test --filter WeekTests` run?
hint: The last line of the run.

prompt: Why are New Year's Day, the day after a leap day and a Sunday the arguments of the second test?
hint: Where does calendar code break?

choices.text: They are boundaries, where calendar bugs live
choices.why: Right: a year, a month and a week each end there.

choices.text: They are the days the planner's users study most
choices.why: Nothing in the course measures that; they are chosen for the arithmetic.

choices.text: Swift Testing allows only three pairs per test
choices.why: The first test has seven arguments.

choices.text: The formula is only wrong on those three days
choices.why: The broken formula failed on every day it was given.

prompt: With `(weekday + 6) % 7`, what did `mondayOf("2026-11-01")`, a Sunday, return?
hint: Sunday is 1; work out (1 + 6) % 7.

choices.text: `2026-10-26`, the right Monday
choices.why: That is what the test expected, and did not get.

choices.text: `2026-10-25`, one day too far back
choices.why: That is what most days did; the Sunday went the other way.
Right: `back` became 0, so the Sunday counted as its own Monday.

choices.text: Nothing: the test crashed
choices.why: It returned a value; the `↳` lines printed it.

prompt: With the formula broken, how many issues did the boundary test, `crossing`, record?
hint: Count the `✘ … recorded an issue` lines, or read the summary.

prompt: `@Test(arguments:)` runs the function once per element, and the report calls each run a test ___.
hint: `with 7 test …`

prompt: Why does `loadWeek` take `some PlanSource` rather than a server client?
hint: What does the test hand it?

choices.text: Because a protocol makes the code run faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: So that a test hands it a source it controls
choices.why: Right: a fixed plan, or a source that fails every time.

choices.text: Because servers are not allowed in Swift packages
choices.why: Lesson 12 talks to a server from a package.

choices.text: `some` makes the function work without `await`
choices.why: It is still `async`; `some` is about the type.

prompt: Where does the `await` go when expecting an async function to throw?
hint: The closure inside the macro is async.

choices.text: Nowhere: `#expect(throws:)` waits on its own
choices.why: The test has to await the macro, because its closure is async.

choices.text: Only inside the closure, before `loadWeek`
choices.why: It is inside too, and the macro itself also needs one.

choices.text: In front of the macro, and before the call inside it
choices.why: Right: `await #expect(throws:) { try await … }`.

choices.text: After the closure, as `#expect(...) await`
choices.why: `await` always comes before what it waits for.

prompt: `aFailedLoadIsPassedOn` checks that the error reaches the caller unchanged. Why is that test the one usually missing?
hint: A real server fails only on a bad day.

choices.text: Errors cannot be compared in Swift Testing
choices.why: `Offline` is `Equatable`, and the test compares it.

choices.text: Async functions cannot throw on Linux
choices.why: It threw on Linux, and the test passed.

choices.text: Without a fake, the failure path is hard to reach
choices.why: Right, and the error screen depends on it.

choices.text: The happy path covers the error path as well
choices.why: Coverage in section 08 shows the opposite kind of gap.

prompt: Match each piece of XCTest to its Swift Testing counterpart.
hint: The table in section 05.

prompt: Which tests in a new Xcode project have to stay XCTest?
hint: Swift Testing does not drive an interface.

choices.text: Every unit test, since Xcode cannot run Swift Testing
choices.why: Xcode runs both frameworks.

choices.text: The UI tests
choices.why: Right: they are `XCUIApplication`, which is XCTest.

choices.text: Tests of async functions
choices.why: Section 04's async tests are Swift Testing.

choices.text: Tests that compare strings
choices.why: `#expect` compares strings like anything else.

prompt: How does `AddSessionUITests` find the *Add session* button?
hint: It sees only what accessibility exposes.

choices.text: By its position on the screen
choices.why: Positions change with the device; the test uses labels.

choices.text: By calling the view's code directly
choices.why: A UI test runs in another process and cannot see the code.

choices.text: By its accessibility label or ID
choices.why: Right: the label lesson 19 wrote, or an identifier.

choices.text: By the variable name in `SessionForm`
choices.why: Variable names do not exist outside the compiled app.

prompt: Why `waitForExistence(timeout:)` rather than a fixed sleep before the assertion?
hint: A slow machine and a fast one.

choices.text: It returns when the element appears, and fails after the timeout
choices.why: Right: no wasted time on a fast machine, no false failure on a slow one.

choices.text: A sleep is not allowed in XCTest
choices.why: It is allowed; it is just the wrong tool.

choices.text: It makes the app load faster
choices.why: Waiting does not change the app's speed.

choices.text: It restarts the app when the element is missing
choices.why: It returns false; the assertion fails.

prompt: A UI test passes on your Mac and fails on a colleague's with the same code. Which section 06 advice most likely fixes it?
hint: What state was each simulator holding?

choices.text: `continueAfterFailure = false`
choices.why: That clarifies a failure; it does not remove its cause.

choices.text: Start from a known state with a launch argument
choices.why: Right: each simulator held a different plan from earlier runs.

choices.text: More UI tests, to cover the difference
choices.why: More tests with the same flaw fail the same way.

choices.text: Moving the test into the package
choices.why: A UI test needs the app; the package has none.

prompt: Which preview is the section's advice to write first?
hint: The awkward states.

choices.text: An ordinary week, 180 planned and 120 done
choices.why: The ordinary week looks fine by construction.

choices.text: A week with no sessions planned at all yet
choices.why: Right: `planned: 0` is where a progress bar can divide by zero.

choices.text: The app's whole first screen, with a live server
choices.why: A preview that needs the whole app is a warning sign.

choices.text: None: previews are optional decoration
choices.why: They are the fastest way to look at hard states.

prompt: What is the difference between a preview and a test?
hint: One can fail.

choices.text: Previews run on Linux, tests do not
choices.why: The opposite: the tests ran on Linux, previews need Xcode.

choices.text: A preview is looked at and never fails
choices.why: Right: it shows what to fix; a test keeps it fixed.

choices.text: A preview checks the arithmetic, a test the layout
choices.why: A preview checks nothing; it draws.

choices.text: None: `#Preview` is a kind of `@Test`
choices.why: They are separate macros for separate jobs.

prompt: Coverage showed lines 51 and 52 of `Plan.swift` never ran in a test. What do they say?
hint: The end of `add`.

choices.text: That `add` is dead code to be deleted
choices.why: `week/main.swift` runs it; the gap is a missing test.

choices.text: No test adds a valid session and checks it
choices.why: Right: the success path is untested, a missing test with a name.

choices.text: That the line count is wrong on Linux
choices.why: The count is right: every test of `add` expects a refusal.

choices.text: That the package needs 100% before release
choices.why: Coverage is a map, not a target.

prompt: A bug is reported: a session on a Sunday shows in the wrong week. Put the work in order.
hint: Test first, then fix.
items: Write a test with that Sunday that fails
Run it and watch it fail
Run every test and watch them pass
Add the cases beside it as arguments

prompt: Which of these ran on the Linux machine for this lesson? Choose all that apply.
hint: Anything under `Tests/PlannerCoreTests/`.

choices.text: `LegacyTests`, in XCTest
choices.why: Yes: XCTest runs on Linux too.

choices.text: `AddSessionUITests`
choices.why: No: it needs the app and a simulator.

choices.text: The coverage report from `llvm-cov`
choices.why: Yes: the toolchain ships it.

choices.text: The `#Preview` of an empty week
choices.why: No: previews need Xcode's canvas.

prompt: Where should a test of the week's arithmetic live?
hint: Fast, and on any computer.

choices.text: A UI test that reads the total off the screen
choices.why: It would check a sum slowly, and only on a Mac.

choices.text: A preview, with the total in its name
choices.why: A preview never fails.

choices.text: The package's tests
choices.why: Right: where the rule lives, run by `swift test` anywhere.

choices.text: `week/main.swift`, checked by eye
choices.why: A program read by eye is a check you repeat yourself.
